Rashi on Eruvin 12a:11:1.hebrew: וגדולה באחת עשרה - דליכא אלא שלשה מכאן ושלשה מכאן, וקתני: גדולה מותרת:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:11:1.english: And the large [one is] eleven [cubits] - For there are only three [handbreadths] on this side and three on that side, and yet it teaches: The large [courtyard] is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:12:1.english: From the sea - He went up from the sea.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:13:1.hebrew: רבי היא וסבר לה כר' יוסי - דאמר: לחי רחב שלשה טפחים בעי. ורבי יוחנן אליבא דרבנן קאמר, דפס דקאמרי רבנן ארבעה טפחים הוא, ובשני רוחות סגי בשני משהויין:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:13:1.english: It is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - For he says that a side post requires [a width of] three handbreadths. And Rabbi Yochanan was speaking according to [the view of] the Rabbis, [holding] that the board of which the Rabbis spoke is four handbreadths, and from two directions, two minimal amounts suffice.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:15:1.english: It was an inlet of the sea that entered a courtyard - And [the waters] breached the wall in its entirety.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:15:2.hebrew: ולא אצרכוה אלא פס אחד - בראש הכותל, ומותר למלאות מן המים לפנים ממקום המחיצה, ולא אמרינן קא ממלא מכרמלית לרשות היחיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:15:2.english: And they required of him only one post - At the end of the wall, and it is permitted to draw from the water inward of the location of the partition, and we do not say that he is drawing from a karmelit into a private domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:16:1.hebrew: שהקילו חכמים במים - למלאות מהן על ידי תיקון כל שהוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:16:1.english: That the Sages were lenient regarding water - To draw [water] from them by means of any minimal arrangement.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:17:1.hebrew: כדבעא מיניה כו' - אלמא יש להקל במים, שאין במקום אחר. להכי נקט חורבה, דדרכה להיות שם מחיצות תלויות:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:17:1.english: As [Rabbi Tavla] asked him, etc. - Consequently, there is a leniency regarding water that does not apply elsewhere. That is why he specified a ruin, as it is typical for there to be suspended partitions there.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:17:2.hebrew: אלא במים - כגון גזוזטרא שהיא למעלה מן הים, בפרק כיצד משתתפין (לקמן עירובין ד' פז:):
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:17:2.english: Only with water - Such as a balcony that is above the sea, in the chapter "Keitzad Mishtatfin" (below, Eruvin 87b).

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:18:1.english: In any case - That [one statement] of Shmuel contradicts [the other statement] of Shmuel.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:19:1.hebrew: פירשוה - לדשמואל: האי דקאמר בפס אחד, היינו ארבעה טפחים, והאי דקאמר שני פסים, בקטנים כל דהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:19:1.english: They explained it - [Namely, the statements] of Shmuel: That which he said, "With one board," that is [a board of] four handbreadths; and that which he said, "Two boards," [is] with small [boards] of any size.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:1:1.english: To Ovelin - [This is the name of] a place.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:21:1.english: Three [handbreadths] and any amount should suffice - For [the breach] is reduced to less than four [handbreadths], and it requires nothing further.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:21:2.english: For Rav Aḥlai said - Above, [where he stated] that [an alleyway of] less than four [handbreadths] does not require anything.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:22:1.hebrew: כאן בחצר - חצר מרובע, או רחבו יותר מארכו. אע"ג דאימעיט מארבעה, לא סגי בהכי:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:22:1.english: Here, in a courtyard - A courtyard is square, or its width is greater than its length. Even though [the breach] has been reduced to less than four [handbreadths], this is not sufficient.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:22:2.english: An alleyway - Its length is greater than its width.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:22:3.hebrew: דרב אחלאי תנאי היא - לקמן מפרש להו, וליכא למיקם עלה דמילתא, הילכך בעינן רוב הדופן עומד:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:22:3.english: [The statement] of Rav Aḥlai is [a dispute between] Tannaim - [The Gemara] explains them below, and it is not possible to determine the matter; therefore, we require the majority of the wall [to be] standing.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:23:1.hebrew: שנכנס לחצר - דרך פירצת הכותל, וכשלא נפרץ במלואו עסקינן, מדמפליג בעשרה ליותר מעשרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:23:1.english: That enters into a courtyard - Through a breach in the wall, and we are dealing with [a case] where [the wall] was not breached in its entirety, since [the baraita] distinguishes between [a breach of] ten [cubits] and more than ten [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:23:2.english: Unless - They made a partition to fence the breach in the courtyard wall [down] to ten [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:23:3.english: But [if it is] ten [cubits], nothing is required - For there is a remnant [of the wall] on this side and on that side.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:24:1.english: It is [only] drawing [water] that we do not draw - Because he carries from a karmelit into a private domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:24:2.english: But carrying we may carry - In this courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:24:3.hebrew: במלואה - לאו דווקא, אלא כל יותר מעשרה קרי ליה מלואה:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:24:3.english: In its entirety - [This is] not literal, but rather, anything more than ten [cubits] is called 'its entirety'.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:6:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר אינו צריך לא לחי ולא קורה כו' - והאי כלום דקאמר, אהנך תוספת דמוספי בית שמאי ורבי אליעזר אדבית הלל קאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:6:1.english: This is what it is saying: It does not require a side post nor a beam, etc. - And this "anything" that he said refers to those additions that Beit Shammai and Rabbi Eliezer add over [the requirements of] Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:7:1.hebrew: וכמה - יהא פחות רוחבו מארבע אמות, ויהא צריך תיקון:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:7:1.english: And how much - May its width be less than four cubits and [still] require rectification?

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:7:2.hebrew: עד ארבעה - טפחים. אפילו אינו רחב אלא אמה, או חמשה או ארבעה טפחים, צריך לחי, אבל בפחות מארבעה אינו צריך כלום:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:7:2.english: Up to four - Handbreadths. Even if it is only a cubit, or five or four handbreadths wide, it requires a side post; but with less than four, it requires nothing.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:8:1.hebrew: בפסי חצר - אם נפרצה למקום האסור לה, צריכה שיור משני צידיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:8:1.english: With regard to the posts of a courtyard - If it was breached into an area forbidden to it, it requires a remnant [of wall] on both of its sides.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:9:1.hebrew: מאן מודים - דקאמר ר' ירמיה? רבי. ומאי הלכתא דקאמר רב נחמן? דמשמע מכלל דפליגי אף בפסי חצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 12a:9:1.english: Who concede - [Who is it] that Rav Yirmeya stated [concedes]? Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]. And what is [the significance of] "the halakhah" that Rav Naḥman stated? That it implies: by inference, they dispute even concerning the upright boards of a courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 12a:9:2.english: Who disagrees with him? The Rabbis - The disputants of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].

Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:21:1.hebrew: וכי תימא בדופן שבעה דבארבעה הוי רוב דופן - והשתא, אי נקט "ארבעה", לא הוי משמיענו חדוש יותר מב"רוב דופן", דאדרבה: השתא דנקט "ברוב דופן", הוי רבותא טפי, דאע"ג דלא הוי ארבעה סגי, הואיל ואיכא רוב דופן. "למה לי ארבעה" - פירוש: למה אטעיה להצריך ארבעה? בשלשה ומשהו סגי, דהשתא לא הוי צריך אפילו רוב דופן, כיון שנתמעט האויר מארבעה. ויש ספרים דגרסי: "למה לי רוב דופן", ולפי זה אתי שפיר בפשיטות. ואית ספרים דלא גרסי "רוב דופן", אלא: "למה לי? בתלתא ומשהו סגי", והיא היא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:21:1.english: And if you say, in [the case of] a wall of seven [handbreadths], where with four it is the majority of the wall - And now, had [Shmuel] stated "four," he would not have taught us any greater novelty than by [stating] "the majority of the wall"; on the contrary, now that he stated "the majority of the wall," it is an even greater novelty, since even though it is not four [handbreadths], it suffices, because there is a majority of the wall. [As for the question,] "Why do I need four?" — the explanation is: Why did [Shmuel] mislead him into requiring four? Three [handbreadths] and a fraction should suffice, for now he would not need even a majority of the wall, since the open space has been reduced to less than four [handbreadths]. And there are books that read: "Why do I need the majority of the wall?" And according to this, it works out well and simply. And there are books that do not read "the majority of the wall," but rather: "Why do I need [this]? With three and a fraction it suffices!" And this is one and the same.

Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:8:1.hebrew: בפסי חצר - וקשה, דגבי מבוי נקט לשון לחי, וגבי חצר נקט לשון פס בכולה שמעתה, אף על גב דשניהם משהו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:8:1.english: With regard to the boards of a courtyard - And it is difficult, for regarding an alleyway [the Gemara] employs the term "side post" [leḥi], and regarding a courtyard it employs the term "board" [pas] throughout the entire discussion, even though both of them [need only be] of a minimal size [mashehu].

Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:9:1.hebrew: ורב נחמן אמר הלכה כר' אליעזר בפסי חצר - והא דלא קאמר: הלכה כרבי בפסי חצר, דהא סבר כרבי אליעזר, כדקאמרינן: ומודים חכמים, היינו רבי, לר' אליעזר, והוה ניחא טפי דאיהו איירי בחצר — אלא דניחא ליה למנקט ר' אליעזר שנזכר במשנתנו. וצריך לומר דרבי ורבנן בחצר מרובעת פליגי, דלרבנן סגי להו בפס משהו, ולרבי צריך שני פסין של שני משהויין. דאי בארכה יתר על רחבה פליגי — קשיא דרב נחמן אדרב נחמן! דהכא פסיק כרבי, ובסוף שמעתא קאמר רב נחמן: נקיטינן דחצר שארכה יתר על רחבה ניתרת בלחי משהו! אלא ודאי במרובע פליגי, וצריך שני פסין של שני משהויין, או בפס אחד של ארבעה, כדאמר רב נחמן בסוף שמעתא: דחצר מרובעת ניתרת בפס ארבעה. ודלא כפירוש הקונטרס שפירש בסמוך: מרוח אחת בד', משתי רוחות משהו לכאן ומשהו לכאן — דהוי כרבנן, דלרבנן סגי בפס אחד ומשהו כדפירשנו; אלא כרבי אתי, דהכי הילכתא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 12a:9:1.english: And Rav Naḥman said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer regarding the upright boards of a courtyard - And as for the fact that he did not say: 'The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] regarding the upright boards of a courtyard' — since he holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, as we say: 'And the Sages concede' — that is, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] — to Rabbi Eliezer, and it would have been more preferable [to cite Rabbi], as he explicitly dealt with a courtyard — [the reason is] that it was preferable to him to cite Rabbi Eliezer, who is mentioned in our Mishnah. And one must say that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and the Rabbis disagree regarding a square courtyard: for according to the Rabbis, an upright board of any minimal size suffices for them, whereas according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], two upright boards of two minimal sizes are required. For if they disagree regarding [a courtyard whose] length exceeds its width, there is a contradiction between [one ruling of] Rav Naḥman and [another ruling of] Rav Naḥman, as here he rules in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], while at the end of the sugya Rav Naḥman says: 'We hold that a courtyard whose length exceeds its width is permitted with a side post of any minimal size.' Rather, they certainly disagree regarding a square [courtyard], and [according to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] it requires two upright boards of two minimal sizes, or one upright board of four [handbreadths], as Rav Naḥman says at the end of the sugya that a square courtyard is permitted with an upright board of four [handbreadths]. And [this is] not like the explanation of Rashi, who explained nearby [that the resolution]: '[If] from one side, with four [handbreadths; if] from two sides, any minimal amount here and any minimal amount there' is in accordance with the Rabbis — for according to the Rabbis, a single board of a minimal amount suffices, as we explained; rather, it conforms to [the view of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], for such is the halakha.
